subject: Tailwind runway sizing & egress mitigation
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Tim Liu <tim.liu@acmecloud.com>, ops-eng@acmecloud.com
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 15 Jun 2025 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Tailwind runway sizing & egress mitigation

Tim / ACME ops team —

Following our onboarding call last week, we ran an initial sizing pass for Tailwind's private deployment to make sure the reserved GPU pool meets your QPS and latency targets while staying inside your egress policy. Attaching the baseline model and a quick diagram. High-level notes: 

- Target steady-state throughput: 1.2k requests/min (burst to 4k requests/min windowed).
- P95 latency goal for generation path: <= 250ms (tail bucket budgeting described in spreadsheet).
- Recommended compute: 8x A10G-equivalent GPUs with continuous batching and a warm pool of 2 nodes for fast burst absorb.
- Network: plan assumes 25 Gbps egress headroom per rack; we need confirmation of cross-rack east-west throughput for shard replication.

Open questions for ACME:
1) Can you confirm the egress cap per cluster and any hard limits on per-connection bandwidth?
2) Expected cold-start SLA for model loads (do you allow pre-warmed kernels persist for 30–60m)?
3) Any procurement window constraints for additional NICs or link aggregation?

Action requested: Tim — please review attached "tailwind-runway-model.xlsx" and the diagram, and confirm egress limits and whether we can schedule a 30m network topology walkthrough this week.

Thanks,
Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
E: evelyn.hart@redwood.ai | M: +1 415-555-0147

Attachments: tailwind-runway-model.xlsx (spreadsheet), egress-topology-diagram.png (PNG diagram)

From: Tim Liu <tim.liu@acmecloud.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops-eng@acmecloud.com, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 15 Jun 2025 14:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Tailwind runway sizing & egress mitigation

Thanks Evelyn — helpful start. Quick answers from our side: 

- Cluster egress cap: currently 40 Gbps per rack, but we have an upcoming maintenance window the week of 6/23 that could temporarily reduce that if we don't bump links.
- Hard per-connection limit: 10 Gbps (we can do LAG but per-flow still 10 Gbps unless we do active-active sharding).
- Cold-starts: we prefer to avoid long-running pinned kernels for security audits, but a 30m warm window for pre-loaded model state during peak windows is acceptable under an exception.

We can do a topology walkthrough Tues 6/17 at 11am PT. Ops will bring a current peering diagram and egress metrics.

--Tim
Tim Liu
Platform SRE Lead, Acme Cloud

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tim Liu <tim.liu@acmecloud.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Jun 2025 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Tailwind runway sizing & egress mitigation

Looping in our provisioning and network sizing notes before the walkthrough. Key changes to Evelyn's baseline after a quick simulation: 

- Given ACME's per-flow 10 Gbps limit, our burst model needs cross-rack multiplexing. We'll split traffic across 3 logical shards to avoid single-flow oversubscription — this increases per-request overhead ~6%.
- Revised compute recommendation: 10x A10G-equivalent GPUs (or 6x A100-80GB if they can tolerate higher per-node cost) to maintain the 250ms P95 when sharded.
- Warm pool sizing: keep 2 nodes hot, add a transient warm-up queue for up to 6 nodes during an extended burst (windowed over 3–5 minutes).
- Admission control: propose soft-shed at 2.5k rps sustained with gradual ramp to preserve KV cache hit rates; the sheet models token-cost per request with binning.

I'll present this on Tues. Karthik — please bring the autoscaler policy variant that prioritizes latency over utilization for private clusters. Marissa — can you double-check the quantization profile assumptions that feed the token cost table?

-Laura

Laura Bennett
Sr. Product PM, Private Deployments | Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tim Liu <tim.liu@acmecloud.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 17 Jun 2025 11:16:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Tailwind runway sizing & egress mitigation

Thanks — notes from the ops walkthrough: 

- ACME network team confirmed 40 Gbps per rack and the 10 Gbps per-flow limit. They flagged a potential maintenance window (6/23) where one of the uplinks will be reduced to 20 Gbps for 6 hours; we've accounted for that by modeling a degraded-case with 50% egress headroom reduction.
- For autoscaling: propose a two-tier policy 
  1) Fast-absorb warm pool (2 nodes) for <30s microbursts — instant attach.
  2) Elastic ramp for multi-minute peaks — scale in 1 node increments with a 90s cool-down; pre-warm kernels in parallel to deployment attach to shave cold-starts.
- Admission and fallback: when egress or compute is constrained, route 15% of traffic to a smaller quantized model variant with slightly higher latency but lower egress/cost. This preserves availability for high-value requests.

Action items assigned:
- Karthik: push autoscaler policy draft to the shared Drive by EOD Tue.
- Marissa: validate quantization impact on fidelity for the 15% fallback cohort.
- Evelyn: confirm post-maintenance window runbook changes and sign-off on the warm-pool config.

Karthik

Karthik Iyer
Staff Engineer, Runtime & Scaling | Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tim Liu <tim.liu@acmecloud.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Jun 2025 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Tailwind runway sizing & egress mitigation

Quick results from the fidelity check on the fallback quantized variant: 

- End-to-end quality regression measured on the evaluation prompt set shows a mean BLEU-like score drop of ~2.9 points for the 15% cohort — acceptable for chat summarization and most classification use-cases, marginal for code-completion/LLM-copilot use-cases.
- Token-rate savings: ~32% lower egress per request on average vs. full model; reduces rack egress pressure significantly during degraded scenarios.

Recommendation: we enable the fallback routing (15%) with a per-route override so product teams can opt out if fidelity-sensitive. I'll upload the full evaluation CSV and the changed quant profiles to the Drive.

Marissa

Marissa Cole
Applied ML Engineer, Model Ops | Redwood Inference
